hypendev · Nov 14, 2026

Ironically, did the same thing and ended up with the same answer.

From wearing a CGM, whoop, using an impedance analyzing scale (I know, I know), blood tests - all the data shows pretty much the same correlation. I mostly did it for fun, but also because I wanted to "figure out how different things impact my body".

While yes, there were some interesting discoveries like: - Some things raise my blood glucose more than I'd expect, pasta for example - those were the things I usually "knew" and foods I'd avoid eating.

- Sleep quality only had correlation with amount of activity/time I went to sleep, so my food and caffeine choice didn't impact it much.

The results were pretty much: Eating bad and moving less is bad for you. Eating good and moving more is good. What your intuition tells you is healthy and good for you, usually is. What it says isn't, usually isn't.

Could have saved me some time and money, but at least I had fun.
